short: The iconic German triplane renowned for its extreme maneuverability and association with the "Red Baron".
full:
Entering operational service in August 1917, the Fokker Dr.I Dreidecker was a German fighter designed in direct response to the maneuverable British Sopwith Triplane. Its distinctive three-wing configuration provided exceptional lift, resulting in an unmatched rate of climb and phenomenal turning ability at lower altitudes. Powered by a rotary engine and armed with twin Spandau machine guns, it was a lethal close-quarters dogfighter.

Despite its agility, the Dr.I suffered from structural deficiencies and was relatively slow compared to contemporary Allied fighters like the S.E.5a and SPAD S.XIII. Its fame is largely inseparable from Manfred von Richthofen, who scored his final nineteen victories in the type before his death in April 1918. By the time of the armistice in November 1918, the triplane had already been largely superseded by the superior Fokker D.VII, and the remaining examples were subsequently dismantled or surrendered.
